messages.subject: Re: Legend Background Width
parts:
I think I forgot to include an important detail in my original post...
see legend only gets messed up when I generate my plots with tikZ via
Sweave. The only work around for now is manually tell ggplot2 to
explicitly assign a desired width for background.

I have had this issue when generating plots with tikZ and what I do
with R base graphics is manually set legend width using 'text.width'.
Please see example code below. What I have been looking for is the
ggplot2 equivalent of base graphics 'text.with' legend attribute

dataset <- c(20, 10)
barplot(dataset, las=2, col=rainbow(2))
legend("topright", c("Male", "Female"), text.width=1)

Lighton Phiri
http://lightonphiri.org

messages.subject: Re: Legend Background Width
parts:
Ah, I see. Is tikZ still working? I gave up on it since it appears to
be unmaintained for some time now.

Anyway, sorry for my incorrect original suggestion. You're right that
legend.key.width controls the actual legend key, not the legend
itself. I don't see a way to change the size of the whole legend using
theme elements, but you can force it using something like

fill=paste(Concept, " ")

Hope that helps,
Ista

messages.subject: Re: Legend Background Width
parts:
>Hope that helps,
It sure did, thank you very much Ista; forgot all about good old
'paste' command. I had to make a minor change though... seeing that
tikZ converts R code into equivalent LaTeX command, and that spaces
are treated uniformly in LaTeX, I used math mode spacing instead
--primitive, but it works.

paste(Concept, "$\\;\\;\\;\\;$")

\; === large space

> Is tikZ still working?
Yes it is still working; except for a few minor issues like the one
you helped solve.

Thanks again!

Lighton Phiri
http://lightonphiri.org
